title: Would you play this game? Ask me anything. Break my heart please. Astra + Webgl + Tripo + Vite. 100–125 hours.
author: ExtentUpstairs1183
selftext:
Hey guys, i making this to see if this game would be viable and if player would want to play. It will be leveless clash royale with gamebreaking abilities. Like stealing elixir, creating tunnel, in game level up and more to come!

There is no 2d sprit in the live game yet, all shaders and 3d gen. 100–125 hours. I am doing a quality sweep right so something look really ugly.

**My loop** is reference/screenshot or youtube video→ specific change → AI implements → playable browser preview beside the terminal → feedback → repeat. AI handles gameplay code, shaders, Blender export scripts, asset integration, debugging, and targeted tests. Blender handles geometry/materials/animation; a dedicated image-generation agent handles raster work when needed. Vite gives me a fast local preview with live updates, so every AI change goes straight into a playable feedback loop

https://preview.redd.it/l6nowtqctqsh1.png?width=1571&format=png&auto=webp&s=d81dfd262633145825bc1dbff2bee85daabc62c2

The infrastructure makes this practical: deterministic simulation so bugs replay from the same seed; a sandbox API so agents can spawn units, trigger abilities, advance exact frames, and inspect state; matched-camera screenshots for visual comparisons; live inspector controls that save tuning into source JSON. Agents check the actual arena, including movement, grounding, shadows, hits, death, and cleanup. For visual refinement, I sometimes request fresh critic agents to review successive iterations.

Project instructions and short checkpoint notes carry context between sessions. Git worktrees plus cooperative file claims keep concurrent work from colliding. Verification is usually source-data checks and one focused visual pass, with tests where they resolve a specific uncertainty. Most of my input is choosing references, identifying what looks or feels wrong, setting constraints, and steering the next iteration.

replies.author: ExtentUpstairs1183
replies.body:
* **No permanent card levels.** Your cards don’t start stronger because you’ve spent more money or played longer. Leveling happens inside the match and resets afterward.
* **Abilities that change more than damage.** Examples include stealing elixir to disrupt an opponent’s next play and creating tunnels to open alternative attack routes. I would have taunt, role swap between attacker and ally. Assassin that can just attack the back.
* **Progression decisions during the match.** I want investing in upgrades versus deploying more units immediately to be a meaningful choice. For example creating items for units during the game. Exp level to manage stronger unit so i can make a character very strong early, very weak later game.
* **Changing Deck Mid battle.** Yes you can change 3-4 units out of the current roster with supported troops selected before the game.
* **More bridges.** Instead of two lanes there are three. I dont know but it seem more fun
* **No spells like CR.**  You cannot wipe out an entire push with a rocket or high damage aoe card.
* **Slower Card Cycle.** I want this game to feel like your not just spamming the same character. 
* **Choose your own tower.** Basically you will have to play a unit in your current deck to take the role of side and main tower shooter.

comments.author: cxfoulke
comments.body:
First 120 hours is nothing... No large scale game is anything in 120 hours. Ai doesnt change that. thats 2.5 weeks of real work if that. 

Gonna be harsh but currently the visuals look poor. There is no strong visual  throughline drawing you into the gameplay. The enemies blend into the background. The elements are mismatched.  The Countdown is low resolution but the ground is very higher resolution. ATM your game is firmly in the Ai slop territory. 

Nothing you describe in this post really matters for making your game? Like a sandbox api agents can already just make a testing enviroment. 

I feel like alot of the posts im reading on this sub are really overengineering prompting. The Ai can handle the work. Keeping the code from becoming an unmaintable mess and scaling out of control is the issue you need to solve.Not i put 10k lines into context to help it find something it would already be able to do. 

Once your on hour 1000 is your prompt taking 30 minutes and 25 minutes of that time is taken fixing bugs because it tried to make a change but ended up causing 10 tests to fail from changing to colour of water from blue to red. 

  
On game design i would get your mindset out of   Im gonna make X game or Y game  but change it so the fireballs actually bounce off walls and the characters have mohawks. 

Into more of a what can i do to create an experience that surpasses others in some way.

replies.author: Neither_Berry_100
replies.body: I don't vibe code but this looks bad for vibe coding. I've seen what others have done. I could spit out more manually with minimal AI work. Not that I want to make this.

replies.author: ExtentUpstairs1183
replies.body:
Fair hits on the visuals. The contrast and the resolution mismatch were already bugging me. I'm struggling to keep the background detailed without it competing with the gameplay. Any games you'd recommend studying for that? Is League and Hades a good reference?

On testing, I'm curious how you handle it at scale:

1. Once a project's past a few hundred hours, roughly how much of your time goes to test infrastructure vs. features?
2. What's in your fast suite, the checks you run on every change?
3. At what point did a dedicated test/debug API become worth building for you, vs. letting the agent spin up throwaway harnesses?
